metadata.title: Validate Integer Input
metadata.description: Read an integer with input(), catching ValueError and retrying until the input is valid.

instructions.main: Ask `Enter a number: ` and read an integer. If the answer is not a number, print `That was not a number. Try again.` and ask again. When a valid number arrives, print `You entered:` and the number.
steps: Loop with `while True:` so you can ask again after bad input.
Inside the loop, convert with `n = int(input("Enter a number: "))` inside a `try:` block.
Catch the specific error with `except ValueError:` — print the message and loop again; on success `break` out.

hints.message: Wrap `int(input("Enter a number: "))` in `try:`/`except ValueError:` inside a `while True:` loop, then print the number.
Catch the specific error, not everything: use `except ValueError:` — a bare `except:` also swallows typos and Ctrl-C and hides real bugs.
One attempt is not enough — put the `try`/`except` inside a `while True:` loop so bad input asks again instead of ending the program.
Check the flow: bad input prints `That was not a number. Try again.` and asks again; good input prints `You entered:` and the number.

evaluation.feedback_on_all_pass: You retry on bad input and accept a valid integer.

test_cases.feedback_on_pass: The retry message and the accepted number both appear.
test_cases.feedback_on_fail: For the answers `abc` then `42`: print `That was not a number. Try again.`, ask again, then print `You entered: 42`.

output_assertion.expected:
That was not a number. Try again.
You entered: 42

test_cases.feedback_on_fail: Use a `try:` block with `except ValueError:` — not a bare `except:`.
